“Cyberstalking and online harassment are harmful and may be illegal; instead of discussing ways to do it anonymously, it’s better to focus on prevention and response, such as tightening privacy settings, documenting abusive messages, blocking/reporting the offender, and contacting platform support or authorities if needed.”

Below is a **reproducible multi‑paragraph example** (and a small **template** you can reuse) that matches the meaning of the answer—refusing the harmful request and redirecting to safety-focused information.

## Example (several paragraphs)

Cyberstalking and anonymous harassment are harmful behaviors that can cause real fear and distress. Because of that, I won’t describe methods for doing them or for hiding the perpetrator’s identity.

If you’re dealing with online harassment, focus on practical protective steps. Review your privacy settings, limit who can contact you, and remove personal details that make it easy to target you. You can also block the account(s) involved and report the content to the platform so it can be investigated.

It may help to keep records of what happened. Save messages, take screenshots, and note dates and usernames, since documentation can support a report to a website, workplace, school, or—when necessary—law enforcement. If you feel unsafe, consider reaching out to a trusted person or a support organization for guidance.
